headline: THE AGENT WHO SAID "WE HAVE TO SELL THEIRS FIRST" AT 8:07 THIS MORNING JUST REQUESTED A SECOND SHOWING ON 198 RENA FOR 10:30 TOMORROW — the morning the listing agreement expires — and the request is sitting unconfirmed. · DO: confirm the Rena showing, then rule the number · WATCH: the fleet went dark 9:54a–3:20p and the speed-to-lead responder missed a live seller lead.

notes: 🔴 THE FLEET WENT DARK FOR FIVE HOURS AND FORTY-FIVE MINUTES IN THE MIDDLE OF THE BUSINESS DAY — 9:54 AM to 3:20 PM. Every routine then fired at once in a catch-up burst at 3:20–3:31. This is the known failure shape: the fleet only runs while the desktop app is open. The measurable cost today is not theoretical — the five-minute speed-to-lead responder missed roughly sixty-five cycles, and a live seller lead sat unread for five hours and eleven minutes before the 3:30 sweep caught it by hand.

🔴 THE MIDDAY DIGEST NEVER RAN, SO NOTHING REACHED YOU BETWEEN THE MORNING LETTER AND NOW. The 12:15 Delta is the only scheduled midday email and it was inside the dark window. Thirteen findings are queued and undrained, including three status reports from the Operations Manager and a corrected identity on the Rena showing agent. The 6:15 PM Delta will drain them.

✅ ONE ALARM THIS BOARD CARRIED ALL MORNING IS NOW DEAD, AND IT WAS KILLED BY EVIDENCE RATHER THAN BY TIME. The 5167 Lake Crest closing was printed here as 'receipted TOMORROW, 8/14, nothing since 8/4.' The date was stale. The real closing is Thursday 8/20 at 3:00 PM, double-receipted off a live calendar event and an executed addendum — the milestone engine caught it before it could fire a congratulations script six days early. That row is now correct.
